newsitem.title: PERU: Rescuers find flight recorder from Peru air crash.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers find flight recorder from Peru air crash.

text.p: U.S. navy frogmen have located the "black box" flight recorder belonging to a Boeing 757- 200 that crashed last week off Peru's Pacific coast killing all 70 people on board, local navy officials said on Wednesday.
Peruvian navy admiral Jorge Teixeira said signals from the instrument were detected 700 feet (213 metres) below the surface at the crash site north-west of the capital Lima.
He added special equipment would now be needed to reach the recorder and check where the rest of the wreckage is. "It could be that the black box has broken away from the fuselage," he said.

The U.S. frogmen were aiding Peruvian navy boats and a submarine using sonar equipment in a rescue operation that began at dawn last Wednesday after the fatal crash of the Aeroperu plane, which was headed from Lima to Santiago, Chile.
The teams have so far recovered only 14 bodies floating on the surface. The other corpses are believed to be still trapped below the sea in the trunk of the plane.
The 70 dead came from Chile, Peru, Mexico, Ecuador, the United States, Italy, Great Britain, New Zealand, Spain, Colombia and Venezuela.
